title: Launch a role headless, with its opening prompt read from a file

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 62c6220 on branch devteam2/sprint-11, in the worktree at /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/fully-completely-devteam2-sprint-11. Sprint file read fresh there immediately before this verdict. Worktree working tree clean.

The code is good. Two things stop it being a PASS: the sprint's own stated deliverable is absent, and there is one demonstrated dead end in the new credential precondition. Neither is a failure of care — Req 5 was flagged honestly rather than faked, which is the behaviour the sprint's Risks section specifically hoped for.

TREE NOTE, worth one line because it is sprint 7 paying off: running status from the main checkout returned "No state file for sprint 11 in /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/fully-completely (branch: main)". That message told me instantly I was in the wrong tree instead of letting me report sprint 11 as never started. That is the exact four-wrong-readings defect sprint 7 fixed, working. Audited and recorded in the worktree.

================================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — REQ 5, THE SPRINT'S STATED DELIVERABLE, IS NOT DONE
================================================================

Req 5's own words: "Discover the six per-role opening prompts by running them. **This is the sprint's deliverable; the flag is the easy half.**" Its criterion: "this cannot be cleared by reading." Team Assignments: "Req 5 is the bulk of the work."

There are no six prompts. Nothing was derived from a headless run, and I am not marking that against Dev Team: the blocker is a missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, confirmed empirically here too, and the user authorized building the rest. Flagging it openly instead of writing six plausible prompts from a desk is exactly what the sprint's Risks section asked QA1 to watch for, and the honest outcome is better than the fabricated one. But user authorization to proceed is not the same fact as the requirement being met, and this gate records what is true.

WHY THIS IS A CONDITIONAL AND SPRINT 10'S REQ 6 WAS NOT. In sprint 10 the blocker was a Windows machine — nobody at any gate in this environment could clear it, so a CONDITIONAL would have created an unclearable precondition with no recovery path, which this framework has a named rule against. This one is different in the way that matters: an API key and a spend authorization are things the USER can supply, today, from here. There is a real, named, clearable path. That is what makes CONDITIONAL the correct instrument rather than a punishment.

It also costs nothing. The sprint is blocked from shipping anyway — Dependencies hold it until 0.1.10 ships and the registry freeze lifts — and it is already parked at dev_build, where this verdict leaves it. There is no schedule cost to being accurate here, which is precisely when accuracy is cheapest and least excusable to skip.

WHAT CLEARS IT: a credential and a spend decision from the user, then the six runs, then the fixed-vs-template determination Req 5 explicitly asks for ("Answer explicitly whether these are fixed per role or templates parameterized by the work — a headless QA1 needs to know which sprint it is auditing"). That question is unanswered and it is the substantive half.

DO NOT ROUTE THIS TO LIVEQA AS A SUBSTITUTE. LiveQA's criterion says "This is Req 5's verification" — verification of six prompts that do not exist yet is not verification, it is LiveQA doing the discovery under a different name. Req 5 gets done here, then LiveQA verifies it.

================================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking, small) — THE CREDENTIAL PRECONDITION IS A DEAD END FOR apiKeyHelper
================================================================

run-role.js:189. Demonstrated, not argued:

  env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY node scripts/launcher/run-role.js qa1 --headless --prompt-file <path>
  -> ERROR: ...Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and re-run, or configure apiKeyHelper via --settings
     (this check does not detect that case, only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
     exit 1

Three things are wrong with that, and they compound:
  1. It is a hard fail() with exit 1 and there is no bypass flag. A project authenticating via apiKeyHelper — which the pinned notes confirm is a first-class supported --bare credential source, not an exotic one — cannot use headless at all.
  2. The message offers "configure apiKeyHelper via --settings" as the remedy, and doing that changes nothing, because the check reads only process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The user follows the instruction and hits the identical error.
  3. --settings is not plumbed through anywhere. headlessLaunchArgs builds ['--agent', id, '--agents', json, '-p', '--output-format', 'json', '--bare', prompt] — grepped, there is no --settings pass-through in this file at all. So even a user who knows what they are doing has no way to supply it through this launcher. The remedy the message names does not exist on this code path.

The code comment calls this "this warning" (run-role.js:186) while the code is a hard exit 1. The comment misdescribes its own severity.

This is Req 4's own failure mode turned around: the requirement is "fails legibly without them", and this fails illegibly WITH them. It is also, again, a precondition the role that hits it cannot clear.

REQUIRED FIX, and the shape is your call: either drop the precondition and let --bare's own failure surface (the pinned notes confirm it is well-formed and legible — is_error true, "Not logged in · Please run /login" — and this sprint's Out of Scope says we emit and do not parse, so nothing here needs to inspect it), or make it a stderr warning rather than a hard fail, or plumb --settings through and detect apiKeyHelper. What must not survive is a hard block whose stated remedy the code rejects.

================================================================
EVERYTHING ELSE — VERIFIED, AND MOSTLY VERY GOOD
================================================================

REQ 2 — MET, and this is the one the criterion warned a diff would hide, so I did not read it. Traced every write path first: run-role.js contains exactly two console calls, both console.error (fail() at :49, the --restart line at :276); the probe uses stdio:'ignore'; the child uses stdio:'inherit'. agents.js, prompts.js, claude-cmd.js, session.js and auth.js contain zero stdout writes between them.
Then ran it, with a fake claude on PATH printing an envelope to stdout and noise to stderr, capturing the two streams to separate files:
    stdout: {"type":"result","is_error":false,"result":"pong","total_cost_usd":0}   PARSES CLEANLY
    stderr: held the noise, nothing else leaked
    --restart path: stdout PARSES CLEANLY there too
The named offender is fixed and the fix is belt-and-braces — headless returns before the restart branch is reachable at all, and the line was moved to stderr anyway. That is the right instinct for a line whose whole failure mode is "somebody later routes into it".

REQ 1 — MET, and I read it looking for the loophole specifically. Headless goes through the same spawnClaude() and the same child_process.spawn() the interactive path already used; it is one OS process running one role, and there is no path by which a role invokes another. The comment states the CLAUDE.md prohibition as the reason rather than leaving it implicit, which is what Req 1 actually asked for.

REQ 3 — MET in substance, and the substance is what matters. All three failure modes name the file or the missing flag:
    missing file -> "Could not read --prompt-file '<path>': ENOENT... Headless mode needs the opening prompt in a real, readable file."
    empty file   -> "--prompt-file '<path>' is empty. Headless mode needs a real opening prompt."
    no flag      -> "--headless requires --prompt-file <path>."
Note for the record: read literally, "the prompt never transits argv" is not true — it is the last element of the child's spawn argv. Read against its own stated rationale (shell command-substitution), it is fully satisfied: an array-based spawn never goes through a shell, and the flag this script exposes is --prompt-file, so no external caller is invited to concatenate free text into a command line. The comment makes exactly this distinction and makes it correctly. I am not raising it; a criterion is satisfied by its purpose, and I would rather say so than pretend the literal wording was met.

REQ 4's FACTUAL BASIS — CHECKED AGAINST PRIMARY SOURCE, as the criterion demands. I read /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/Fifty_Mission_Cap/metering/output-format-json-notes.md at 39a12fd directly, not from this sprint file or the handoff. It says what is claimed: --bare "strictly requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper — OAuth and keychain auth are explicitly not read", and an unauthenticated --bare attempt produced is_error true with "Not logged in · Please run /login" while the envelope stayed well-formed with the same top-level shape, zeroed values and no modelUsage. --bare is passed unconditionally with no opt-out, so headless cannot inherit the operator's OAuth session. The isolation half of Req 4 is correct; only the precondition (Finding 2) is wrong.

REQ 6 — MET, and it is a runnable check rather than a claim. The argv builders are pure and exported, and I asserted against them myself rather than trusting the suite: freshLaunchArgs produces exactly the pre-sprint shape, byte-identical to what 93471c0's inline array built; resumeLaunchArgs produces ['--agent','qa1','--resume',uuid] for a normal role and appends devTeam2ResumePrompt only for dev-team-2 — I got that assertion wrong on my first pass (expected 4 elements, it is correctly 5) and the code was right, not me. Guarding main() with require.main === module is the correct way to make this testable without changing CLI behaviour.

REQ 7 — MET, read cold. Both files name the trigger characters explicitly ("backticks, `$`, or code of any kind"), state the action (write to a file, use --notes-file), cite the real incident rather than a hypothetical, and tell the reader not to improvise a shorter direct invocation that skips the command file's own pattern. That last clause is the one that will actually prevent recurrence.

REQ 9 — MET, run not read. 99 OK lines, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED.
verify-tarball.sh: TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, launcher files match live source, sprint data clean, baseline table present.

REQ 8 — HELD, CORRECTLY, AND THE SPRINT FILE CONTRADICTS ITSELF. package.json is 0.1.10. Req 8 says bump to 0.1.11; Dependencies says "Hold the version bump until ship time if 0.1.10 has not gone out yet — Req 8 and sprint 10's Req 7 edit the same line." 0.1.10 has not shipped. Dev followed Dependencies, which is the right call, and the acceptance criterion for Req 8 is therefore unsatisfiable as written today. Recording it as a specification contradiction rather than a defect: Master Controller should reconcile the two, and Req 8 must be done before this ships regardless.

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL — NOT REQUIRED FIXES
================================================================

1. QUANTIFIED CEILING NOBODY HAS NOTICED. The --agents payload puts the entire persona body in the child's argv. Measured all six: master-controller 10,778 chars, qa1 9,718, dev-team-2 9,493, pipeman 8,925, liveqa 8,418, dev-team-1 8,397. Full argv worst case ~10,845 chars against Windows' 32,767-char CreateProcess limit, leaving ~21,900 shared with the opening prompt. Fine today. Agent files grow every sprint — this sprint alone added to two of them — and sprint 10 just made Windows a first-class target, so this is a real budget with a real limit and it is currently uncounted. If a role's persona and its opening prompt ever approach that together, headless fails on Windows only, which is the exact platform-asymmetric failure class sprint 10 existed to end.

2. The interactive path's check ORDER changed: the operator auth check used to run before the agent-file existence check and now runs after it. Only observable when both fail at once, where the user now sees the agent-file error instead of the auth error. Not a regression in function and Req 6's criterion is about the path still working, which it demonstrably does. Worth knowing it moved.

3. Unverified and correctly flagged by Dev: whether `model` inside the --agents JSON is honored or silently ignored. Needs a credentialed run — same blocker as Req 5, and it should be answered in the same pass rather than as a separate errand.

4. For sequencing, observed in the main checkout, not this worktree: sprint 10's QA1 PASS bookkeeping (registry.json and state/sprint-10.json) is still uncommitted on main. Under sprint 9's release ordering that is fine and arguably correct, but somebody should know it is sitting there before shipping 0.1.10.

CODE QUALITY

Test coverage: 99 passing; the CLI-level headless tests use a fake claude on PATH, so they cost nothing and still exercise the real process boundary — the right design for this.
Error handling: every headless failure names the file, the flag, or the missing credential. fail() is stderr-only throughout.
Standards: agentBody() reuses parseFrontmatter's own regex match rather than a second copy, with the reason stated; readAgentMeta gained a field additively; pure argv builders extracted rather than duplicated. The persona can never be described differently by the two launch paths, which was the right thing to guarantee.
Security: the --prompt-file design is correct and the comment reasons about it accurately, including being clear that this file's own spawn is not the exposure.
Reporting accuracy: the handoff's claims all held up — zero console.log, tests green, tarball passing, and the repointed baseline tests were repointed for the stated reason.

RECOMMENDATION

Fix Finding 2 (one function, your call on shape), and get Req 5 done once the user supplies a credential and authorizes the spend — including the fixed-vs-template answer, and item 3 above while the credentials are live. Then come back for round 2. Do not touch anything else: Req 2's stdout discipline and Req 1's process separation are both correct and I do not want them disturbed by an unrelated fix.

Nothing ships regardless until 0.1.10 is out and the freeze lifts, so there is time to do Req 5 properly rather than fast.

CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 2. Audited 40eb6ce on branch devteam2/sprint-11, in the worktree. Sprint file re-read fresh; `git diff 62c6220 HEAD -- docs/sprints/2-in-progress/` is empty, so the requirements are byte-identical to round 1's. Worktree clean.

FINDING 2 — CLOSED. FINDING 1 (Req 5) — STILL OPEN, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS NOT A PASS.

================================================================
FINDING 2 — FIXED PROPERLY, VERIFIED AT THE PROCESS BOUNDARY
================================================================

The complaint was that the error message named a remedy that existed nowhere in the file. It exists now, and I checked it reaches the real spawned process rather than trusting the unit tests. Ran headless with a fake claude that dumps its own argv:

    --agent qa1 --agents <9718 chars> -p --output-format json --bare --settings /tmp/fc11/settings.json "You are QA1. Audit sprint 11."

--settings is genuinely forwarded to claude, and it is positioned before the prompt, which stays the final positional argument — the thing that would have broken silently if it had been appended carelessly. The comment says that constraint out loud and a test asserts it, which is the right pair.

The precondition now behaves correctly in all three states, each run rather than read:
    neither supplied        -> hard fail, and the message now names a remedy that exists,
                               with a copy-pasteable invocation rather than a dangling reference
    --settings alone        -> proceeds, reaches claude with --settings carried through
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY alone -> proceeds, and emits no stray --settings (0 occurrences in argv)
An apiKeyHelper-only project can now use headless. That was the whole defect.

The deliberate limitation is correctly reasoned and correctly documented: a meaningless --settings value ('{}') still passes this check and falls through to --bare's own legible is_error failure. Validating it here would mean re-implementing claude's settings parsing to double-check a thing claude already reports clearly, and Req 4 asks for a legible failure, not specifically an early one. That is the same "don't block on an inconclusive signal" reasoning the interactive checkAuth() path already uses. Right call, and stating the trade rather than hiding it is what makes it reviewable.

NO REGRESSION ANYWHERE I CHECKED:
    run-role.js still contains zero stdout writes (Req 2 intact)
    stdout on a headless run still parses cleanly as JSON with --settings present
    102 OK lines, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED (was 99)
    verify-tarball.sh: TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, launcher files match live source, sprint data clean
The three new tests are CLI-level as claimed — they assert on the real spawned argv and on exact stdout/stderr, not just on the pure builder. One of them asserts stderr is empty on a successful headless run, which is the Req 2 property stated as a test rather than as a comment. Good addition, nobody asked for it.

Round-2 diff scope: two files, run-role.js and launcher_test.js. Nothing else touched, which is what I asked for.

================================================================
FINDING 1 — REQ 5 STILL NOT MET. THE VERDICT STAYS CONDITIONAL ON THIS ALONE.
================================================================

Nothing has changed here and nothing should have: there are still no six per-role opening prompts, and the fixed-versus-template question Req 5 explicitly asks is still unanswered. The sprint's own words are that this is the deliverable and the flag is the easy half. A sprint whose stated deliverable is absent is not a PASS, and no amount of quality in the other half changes that.

TO BE CLEAR ABOUT WHOSE CALL IS WHOSE, because the handoff put this to me as "your decision": the verdict shape is mine and it is CONDITIONAL. Whether to spend money on a credentialed discovery pass is the USER'S call, not QA1's — I do not authorize spend, and I am not going to pretend that recording a verdict is the same as making that decision. What I can say is that the requirement is unmet, that it is clearable (an API key and a spend authorization, both things the user controls), and that until it is done this sprint is not finished.

DEV TEAM'S HANDLING OF IT IS CORRECT AND SHOULD NOT CHANGE. Refusing to guess at spend authorization and refusing to fabricate six plausible prompts is exactly what the sprint's Risks section hoped for and exactly what the epic exists to enforce. Two rounds of holding that line under pressure to close is worth more than the prompts themselves.

THIS COSTS NOTHING. The sprint cannot ship until 0.1.10 is out and the registry freeze lifts, and it is already parked at dev_build, where this verdict leaves it. There is no schedule being protected by calling this done early.

WHAT ROUND 3 NEEDS, once the user supplies a key and authorizes the spend:
  - the six per-role opening prompts, derived from actual headless runs, in a throwaway git-init directory with a published install, never in this repo (the sprint's own Dependencies say so, and driving a real sprint through both gates here would pollute this project's sprint history)
  - the explicit fixed-vs-template answer, and if templates, what the caller must supply — a headless QA1 has to be told which sprint it is auditing, which interactive initialPrompt(role.label) never had to convey
  - while the credentials are live, settle whether `model` inside the --agents JSON is honored or silently ignored. Still unverified, still correctly flagged, and it is the same blocker — do it in the same pass rather than as a second errand later.

================================================================
STILL OPEN FROM ROUND 1, UNCHANGED, NOT REQUIRED FIXES
================================================================

1. Req 8 (0.1.11) still correctly held at 0.1.10 per Dependencies, and the sprint file still contradicts itself between Req 8 and Dependencies. Master Controller reconciles; the bump happens at ship time regardless.
2. The --agents argv budget: master-controller's payload is 10,778 chars against Windows' 32,767 limit, ~21,900 shared with the prompt. Unchanged this round. Still uncounted, still growing every sprint.
3. The interactive path's auth-check / agent-file-check order swap. Observable only when both fail at once.
4. Sprint 10's PASS bookkeeping still sitting uncommitted on main, for whoever sequences the 0.1.10 release.

RECOMMENDATION

Hold at dev_build. Finding 2 is closed and I have no further code findings — do not touch run-role.js again for this sprint unless Req 5's runs turn something up.

The next move is the user's, not Dev Team's and not mine: supply a credential and authorize the spend, or decide Req 5 is deferred out of this sprint entirely — which would be a scope change to the sprint file and Master Controller's to make, on the record, not something this gate absorbs by passing it quietly.

CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 3. Audited 8733319 on branch devteam2/sprint-11, in the worktree. Sprint file re-read fresh: it WAS amended (9833cf2) — Reqs 3, 4 and 5 rewritten, Reqs 10 and 11 added, Req 4 reversed in direction. Audited against the current file. Worktree clean.

Req 10 and Req 11 are done and verified. Three things stop this being a PASS, and the first one is the serious one.

================================================================
FIRST — A REQUEST I AM DECLINING, AND IT IS NOT A PROCEDURAL REFUSAL
================================================================

The handoff hands me a diff to apply "from wherever you have the access." No. I do not write or modify code — but that is the smaller half of the reason.

The larger half: that change was blocked three times by Claude Code's own safety classifier, with an explicit instruction to stop rather than route around it. Handing it to a different actor to apply IS routing around it. It does not matter that the reasoning behind the flag is sound, that the blockage is inconvenient, or that I would be the one typing it. A control that can be cleared by asking a different session is not a control.

And on the merits, this is not a formality worth waving through. `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` removes every permission prompt from an unattended agent that writes files and executes scripts in whatever directory it lands in. That is a genuine security decision with a real blast radius, and it is exactly the kind of decision that should be made explicitly, on the record, by the user — with Master Controller scoping it into a requirement — rather than applied quietly by whichever role happened to have write access. Dev Team stopping when told to stop was correct. Escalating it as a finding was correct. The next move is the user's, in the open, not mine in the dark.

Recording this here so the refusal is on the durable record and not only in a handoff message.

================================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — REQ 5'S PROVENANCE COMMENT CLAIMS SOMETHING THE HANDOFF SAYS DID NOT HAPPEN
================================================================

scripts/launcher/prompts.js, the comment above headlessScaffold(), states:

  "Discovered by actually running each of the six roles headless, through one throwaway sprint
   driven through both gates in a scratch git-init directory (never this repo), not composed
   from a desk."

The same round's handoff states:

  "A real headless Dev Team 1 run ... proved headless can't write files or run scripts at all —
   every tool call hits an unanswerable permission request."

These cannot both be true. A role that cannot write files cannot record a verdict; a sprint cannot be driven through both gates without verdicts being recorded. The handoff describes one role attempted, blocked at the first tool call. The comment describes six roles completing a full two-gate pass.

I am not guessing which is accurate, and I do not need to: whichever it is, a claim of empirical provenance is sitting in a shipped source file that the sprint's own evidence contradicts. Req 5's acceptance criterion is "this cannot be cleared by reading — confirm the templates came from actual headless runs," and I cannot confirm it. The sprint's Risks section anticipated this exact failure ("The six prompts get written from a desk ... QA1 is told to detect it by tone"). It did not take tone. It took reading two of your own artifacts side by side.

REQUIRED FIX: make the comment say what actually happened. If one role was run and blocked, say that, and say the templates are provisional pending the runs. A provisional template honestly labelled is fine and useful. A desk-written template labelled as empirically derived is the thing this entire epic exists to stop, and it would have shipped to every install.

TO BE FAIR ABOUT WHAT IS GOOD HERE, because the templates themselves are not the problem: I read all six against Req 5's amended criterion — "read every template for restated state ... flag each." There is no restated verdict, note, requirement or phase history anywhere in them. They point at registry.json, the sprint file, and the state file, and the scaffold explicitly says "This message does not restate anything from either." The fixed-scaffold-plus-per-role-pointer shape is exactly what the amended requirement predicted and asked for. The content is right. The provenance claim attached to it is not.

REQ 5 REMAINS UNMET regardless of the comment fix. It is now blocked on the permission-mode decision above rather than on a credential, which is a different blocker with a different owner, but the requirement is still open.

================================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking, small) — THE HANDOFF MISDESCRIBES THIS ROUND'S OWN SCOPE
================================================================

"Reqs 3/4/6/7/9 — re-verified against the current file, unchanged in substance."

Reqs 3 and 4 were substantially reimplemented in this very commit:
  - Req 3 was amended from "read the prompt from a file" to "run-role.js composes the prompt
    itself from a per-role template, parameterized by sprint id, file as override only."
    You implemented that: a new --sprint flag, headlessPrompt(), six templates in prompts.js.
  - Req 4 REVERSED. It previously required credential isolation via unconditional --bare; it now
    requires headless to run on the operator's existing session with no API key needed. You
    implemented that too: --bare is now opt-in, the default path uses --no-session-persistence,
    and checkAuth() gates the default branch.
run-role.js changed 280 lines and prompts.js gained 60. "Unchanged in substance" is the opposite of what happened, and it is the kind of line that would lead an auditor to skip re-reading the two requirements that changed most — which is precisely why I re-read the amendment before the code.

REQUIRED FIX: none in code. Describe the round accurately next time. Recording it because this is the fifth reporting-accuracy item across eleven sprints and it has never once been the code that was wrong.

================================================================
REQ 10 — MET. EXERCISED, NOT READ, EXACTLY AS THE CRITERION DEMANDS.
================================================================

LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT_CODE = 64, and every launcher-level failure lands there with a stderr line naming the specific cause. Ran all five:

  unreadable prompt file        exit 64   names the path and the ENOENT
  unknown role id               exit 64   names the id and lists the valid ones
  missing --sprint              exit 64   names both ways to supply a prompt
  claude not on PATH            exit 64   names the exact command to verify by hand
  --bare with no credentials    exit 64   names both credential sources and a copy-pasteable invocation

Pass-through verified with a fake claude whose exit code I controlled:
  child exits 0 (a completed turn — a recorded verdict, FAIL included) -> launcher exits 0
  child exits 1                                                        -> launcher exits 1

The FAIL-level trap in this requirement is not tripped: a recorded verdict exits 0. That is the case the sprint called "the natural mistake and the most damaging one," and it is handled correctly and for the right reason — a completed turn exits 0 on its own, so pass-through gives the property for free without the launcher parsing the envelope, which keeps Req 2's boundary intact.

The documented gap is honest and correctly placed: a real is_error:true from claude also returns 1, so a refusal and a crashed session are indistinguishable at exit-code level. Req 10 explicitly says do not pass the child's code through without documenting that you have. You documented it, including which case it does not cover. That is the requirement satisfied, not dodged.

I could not run the end-to-end half of this criterion (a real role recording a real FAIL) — same blocker as Req 5. What I verified is the launcher's contract; the model-side half is LiveQA's, and it is already in their criteria.

================================================================
REQ 11 — MET
================================================================

The trigger now reads "If `package.json` has changed since the last ship — check it yourself, don't rely on what the sprint's requirements said at the start." It cites 8f597b8 as the real instance, explains that the bump landed mid-loop rather than in the original requirements, and states that the old wording would have missed it and npm would have rejected the commit. Read against the 8f597b8 case: the new trigger catches it, the old one does not. It fails safe in the right direction too — checking a file is cheap and produces a false positive at worst.

This is the recurrence I flagged in sprint 9's notes and again in sprint 10's, now closed. Worth noting it took a real near-miss to land, which is exactly the evidence threshold this project set for itself.

================================================================
REQS 3, 4, 6, 7, 9 — RE-AUDITED AGAINST THE AMENDED FILE, NOT ACCEPTED AS "UNCHANGED"
================================================================

Req 3 (amended) — MET. --sprint composes the prompt from the per-role template; --prompt-file remains an override and wins when both are given, which the comment correctly justifies as "an explicit override should get exactly what it asked for." Missing both is a launcher failure naming both options. No prompt text is accepted as a CLI argument.

Req 4 (reversed) — MET. --bare is opt-in. The default path passes --no-session-persistence instead and gates on checkAuth(), the same check and the same credential source the interactive path uses — which is right: two different tests of the same fact would drift. A key is optional, not a precondition, which is the reversal. --bare plus its credential precondition survives for a consumer that wants isolation, which the amended requirement explicitly preserves as an option.
  NOT VERIFIED, and it is on the criterion: "side-effect findings were tested rather than read from help text." I see no recorded findings about what --no-session-persistence does and does not suppress (hooks, LSP, plugin sync, attribution, auto-memory). The amended Req 4 says "a documented unsuppressible side effect is acceptable; an assumed-away one is not," and right now they are neither documented nor tested. Not blocking on it separately since it needs the same real runs as Req 5 — do it in that pass.

Req 6 — MET. Pure argv builders still exported; the interactive fresh/resume shapes are still asserted mechanically.
Req 7 — MET, unchanged, still names backticks, $, and code explicitly.
Req 9 — MET. Ran it: 116 OK lines, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED (was 102).
verify-tarball.sh: TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, sprint data clean.
Req 8 — still correctly held at 0.1.10 per Dependencies; the sprint file still contradicts itself between Req 8 and Dependencies. Master Controller reconciles; the bump happens at ship time.

Confirmed this round and worth recording: `model` inside the --agents JSON IS honored, established by a real haiku-model run. That was flagged unverified in rounds 1 and 2 and is now closed.

================================================================
STILL OPEN, NOT REQUIRED FIXES
================================================================

1. The --agents argv budget. Unchanged: master-controller ~10.8k chars against Windows' 32,767 limit, now sharing that budget with a composed prompt rather than an arbitrary one — slightly better, still uncounted.
2. The interactive auth-check / agent-file-check order swap from round 1.
3. Sprint 10's PASS bookkeeping still uncommitted on main, for whoever sequences 0.1.10.

RECOMMENDATION

Two fixes, both small: correct the Req 5 provenance comment to describe what actually ran, and describe the round accurately in the next handoff. Do not touch run-role.js's exit-code logic or the templates' content — both are right.
